hints: Monsters move one step per minute, so first compute each cell's earliest monster arrival time with multi-source BFS.
Then BFS from A, entering a cell only if your arrival time is strictly earlier than monsters' arrival there.
A boundary cell reached safely is an escape; store parent moves to output the path.
analogy: Compute when danger reaches each square, then move through squares only while arriving first.
example: If a monster reaches a corridor cell in 2 steps and A needs 2 steps too, that cell is unsafe because arrival must be strictly earlier.
algorithm: Run BFS from all M cells to fill monsterTime. Run player BFS with time t+1 and require t+1<monsterTime[next]; on reaching a boundary reconstruct and print the path.
correctness: Monster BFS gives the earliest possible threat time; the strict inequality guarantees the player never shares a cell with a monster, and BFS gives a valid shortest escape.
